stories.title: Burnham rules out United Ireland poll during first NI visit
stories.summary: Prime Minister Andy Burnham declared a border poll 'off the table' during his first official visit to Northern Ireland, meeting Stormont's first and deputy first ministers. He focused on resolving the Stormont budget crisis (a £1.6bn shortfall) and pledged to find a solution to fund public services.

stories.title: Burnham visits Wales, meets Tata Steel on reindustrialisation tour
stories.summary: PM Burnham visited south Wales as part of his summer listening tour, meeting Tata Steel Managing Director T.V. Narendran and Welsh Labour leaders to discuss reindustrialisation and cost-of-living pressures. The visit comes as Port Talbot's blast furnaces — shut in 2024 — are being replaced by a £1.25bn electric arc furnace.

stories.title: Burnham drops donations cap and to host Macron next week
stories.summary: The Guardian confirmed Burnham has dropped support for capping political donations after a union lobbying blitz, while Politico broke the scoop that Burnham will host French President Emmanuel Macron in London next week as part of a broader diplomatic reset with Europe.

topics.name: Burnham Gov Intelligence
topics.description: Procurement, tech/AI, spending, vendor & priority signals

stories.title: 🏗️ Capgemini wins £200m HMRC data warehouse contract — total DWIT awards reach £420m
stories.summary: Capgemini has secured a £200m contract (Lot 2) on HMRC's Data Warehouse and Integration Transformation (DWIT) programme, responsible for migrating legacy data warehouses to an AWS data lakehouse. Combined with earlier awards to NTT DATA (£75m), Credera (£100m) and IBM (£45m), total DWIT contract value now stands at £420m. TechMarketView noted this raises questions about HMRC's over-reliance on a single supplier (Capgemini) after a string of recent wins totalling over £800m.

stories.title: 🏗️ Met Police picks UK reseller heavyweights for £370m deals
stories.summary: The Metropolitan Police has selected major UK IT resellers for framework deals worth up to £370m, reflecting continued large-scale public safety technology procurement under the Burnham government.

stories.title: 🤖 Tech leader Megan Lee-Devlin appointed CEO of HM Courts & Tribunals Service
stories.summary: A technology leader has been appointed to head HM Courts and Tribunals Service, signalling continued focus on digital transformation in the justice sector. Separately, the UK Space Agency has funded 16 projects sharing £13m to transform public transport and agriculture using 5G/6G networks.

stories.title: 🤖 Treasury signs £280k deal to accelerate AI adoption in government finance
stories.summary: HM Treasury has signed a £280,000 contract explicitly aimed at accelerating AI adoption in government finance, a signal of the Burnham government's intent to deploy AI across central government functions. The DfE is also working on an EdTech certification regime as the ICO flags data-protection concerns.

stories.title: 🤖 UK public sector spent £1.4bn on AI in 2026 to date — breaking all records
stories.summary: UK public sector AI procurement has hit £1.4bn in 2026 so far, breaking all previous annual records. This signals accelerating government commitment to AI transformation, with implications for vendors and consultancies positioned in the space.

stories.title: 🤝 PwC UK acquires AI data consultancy Datasparq
stories.summary: PwC's Strategy& arm has agreed to acquire London-based AI and data consultancy Datasparq (50–60 staff), focusing on AI engineering, data science, and agentic technologies. The deal will layer Datasparq's capability into PwC's PE and corporate advisory practice, intensifying competition between Big Four firms and IT services players for AI-led consulting mandates.

stories.title: 🚦 Wes Streeting to scrutinise MOD procurement as new Defence Secretary
stories.summary: Wes Streeting has been appointed Defence Secretary and plans to move quickly on MOD reform without getting bogged down in a major review. He will scrutinise individual procurement decisions to identify waste, and is expected to bring in Matt Hood (former DHSC delivery unit head) to his team.

stories.title: 📄 Research Report — Building No. 10 North (Re:State, July 2026)
stories.summary: Re:State think tank published a detailed plan for Andy Burnham's proposed 'Number 10 North' — a new northern devolution hub. Key signals: (1) Proposes four core units including a PM's Transformation Directorate to drive civil service reform; (2) 'Devolve by default' principle — decisions at the most appropriate level, not Whitehall; (3) Civil service reform to reward 'ownership, drive and delivery' over process; (4) Intergovernmental machinery proposed to coordinate No. 10, No. 10 North, and devolved governments; (5) 9-week implementation roadmap for operationalising No. 10 North.

topics.name: Parliament
topics.description: House of Commons, House of Lords, PMQs, debates, legislation

stories.title: Parliament in recess — returns Tuesday 2 September
stories.summary: Parliament is currently in summer recess and returns on Tuesday 2 September 2026. Justice Secretary Alex Norris is expected to announce final details of the early-release scheme on Parliament's first day back, amid controversy over domestic abuse exemptions.

stories.title: Bank of England to get new digital currency legal objective via Lords amendment
stories.summary: The Treasury is handing the Bank of England a new legal secondary objective to boost innovation in digital currencies and payments, via an amendment to the Financial Services and Markets Bill due in the Lords next month. This signals government intent to lead on digital finance regulation.

stories.title: Labour NEC election: voting closes today for nine council seats
stories.summary: Voting closes at noon today for nine seats on Labour's National Executive Committee. Results expected today or Friday. Polling predicts the Centre-Left Grassroots Alliance, Mainstream and Labour to Win candidates are most likely to be elected.

topics.name: Labour Party
topics.description: Labour party news, policy, internal politics

stories.title: Burnham accused of U-turn after dropping donations cap under union pressure
stories.summary: Andy Burnham has dropped his support for capping political donations after a lobbying blitz from Labour's trade union backers, who objected to a proposed cap below £500k. The Guardian and Politico confirmed the reversal, which critics say exposes the PM to charges of being beholden to union interests.

stories.title: McFadden: work is 'part of the answer' to youth mental health crisis
stories.summary: Work and Pensions Secretary Pat McFadden said too often a mental health diagnosis is 'leading to a life on benefits' for young people, as the Jobs Guarantee scheme launched its first placements. ONS figures showed around 1 million young people are not in education, employment or training (NEETs).

stories.title: Green Party closing in on Labour's membership figures
stories.summary: Labour membership stood at 264,754 in 2025, down from over half a million earlier in the decade. New accounts show the Green Party may be close to overtaking Labour's membership, reflecting the ongoing hollowing out of Labour's grassroots.

stories.title: Meloni allies deny telling Badenoch not to ally with Farage
stories.summary: Allies of Italian PM Giorgia Meloni have firmly denied claims briefed by Tory aides that Meloni told Badenoch to 'be your own woman' and avoid a pact with Reform UK. Badenoch herself has refused to deny the Conservatives are plotting a coalition with Reform, amid leaked audio from one of her MPs.

stories.title: Burnham enters autumn with higher approval than Badenoch and Farage
stories.summary: Reuters reports Burnham heads into the autumn parliamentary session from a position of strength, enjoying higher popularity ratings than Kemi Badenoch (Conservatives) and Nigel Farage (Reform UK). However, questions remain over how he will fund his ambitious policy agenda.

stories.title: Shadow WPS Helen Whately tours studios on jobs/NEET figures
stories.summary: Shadow Work and Pensions Secretary Helen Whately toured broadcast studios arguing Labour's employment rights laws and employer National Insurance rise are worsening youth unemployment, as the ONS published NEET figures showing around 1 million young people out of education and work.

topics.name: Liberal Democrats
topics.description: Lib Dem party news and policy positions

stories.title: Ed Davey supports 'parent strike' for better paternity leave in Brighton
stories.summary: Lib Dem leader Sir Ed Davey appeared in Brighton to support a 'parent strike' calling for improved paternity leave rights, using the recess period to campaign on family policy ahead of Parliament's return.

stories.title: Davey calls for councillor suspensions over 'death camp' comments
stories.summary: Sir Ed Davey called for the suspension of Everton fan councillors pending investigation after 'death camp' comments in a dispute over a proposed stadium. Davey also described recent violence in Middlesbrough as 'deeply worrying'.

topics.name: Reform UK
topics.description: Nigel Farage and Reform UK party news

stories.title: Reform hits lowest poll rating in 18 months as Farage faces scrutiny
stories.summary: Reform UK is heading for third place in the polls (23%), just ahead of Labour (22%) and the Conservatives (20%), with polling experts saying Farage is being 'dragged down' by his own leadership. Farage is also facing a parliamentary probe into undisclosed gifts from convicted criminal George Cottrell.

stories.title: Farage faces polling hit from Restore Britain — deal or no deal
stories.summary: Politico analysis shows More in Common polling finds Reform's support actually FALLS if they ally with Rupert Lowe's Restore Britain, putting off 2024 Tory voters and even some 2024 Reform voters. The three-way right-wing competition is playing out in a Dover council by-election today.

stories.title: Danny Kruger: Reform would end taxpayer-funded 'woke' civil service networks
stories.summary: Reform's Danny Kruger announced that a Reform government would force civil service staff networks to meet outside working hours and remain strictly neutral, claiming these networks allow staff to promote 'woke causes and DEI roles' costing over £200m per year.

topics.name: SNP
topics.description: Scottish National Party and Scottish politics

stories.title: Poll: Burnham most popular politician in Scotland as SNP rises to 34%
stories.summary: A new Herald Scotland poll shows Andy Burnham is now the most popular politician in Scotland, even as the SNP has risen from 31% to 34% voting intention. The cross-border popularity of the new PM may complicate SNP messaging on independence.

stories.title: SNP free school bags plan raises cost and education questions
stories.summary: The SNP has announced plans to provide free school bags for every child starting Primary 1 in 2027, but the policy has sparked a political row over its cost and whether it represents good use of public money.

stories.title: Victoria Quay: SNP faces questions over £10m 'ghost ship' building
stories.summary: Victoria Quay has cost Scottish taxpayers nearly £10m since 2021 while much of the building sits unused. Commentators say the SNP must confront the wasted expenditure amid wider scrutiny of public spending in Scotland.

topics.name: Cabinet Office
topics.description: Government reshuffles, senior appointments, cross-department policy

stories.title: MHCLG confirms junior minister portfolios following Burnham reshuffle
stories.summary: The Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local Government has finally confirmed the portfolios of its new junior ministers following the Burnham government reshuffle, with two ministers taking on responsibility for planning casework.

stories.title: Wes Streeting appointed Defence Secretary — plans rapid MOD overhaul
stories.summary: Wes Streeting has taken over as Defence Secretary, aiming to overhaul the MOD without a lengthy review and focusing on identifying procurement waste. He is expected to build on reforms John Healey started while scrutinising individual procurement decisions.

stories.title: National Drought Group convenes with water companies amid flooding paradox
stories.summary: The National Drought Group met today with ministers and water company bosses as 71% of England and all of Wales are officially in drought, even as thunderstorm warnings bring up to a month's worth of rain. Thames Water's status and water industry reform are expected to feature in discussions.

topics.name: Elections & By-elections
topics.description: Upcoming or recent election results, polls

stories.title: Wandsworth Trinity ward by-election today — knife-edge council balance
stories.summary: Voters in Wandsworth Council's Trinity ward head to the polls today in a by-election contest between Conservatives, Labour, Lib Dems, Greens and Reform UK. The result won't change council control but could signal the direction of the borough where balance of power rests on a single seat.

stories.title: Clacton by-election: Farage expected to win but faces parliamentary probe
stories.summary: Nigel Farage is expected to comfortably win the Clacton by-election (triggered after he resigned his seat), but he faces a parliamentary probe into undisclosed gifts from convicted criminal George Cottrell. Defeats in Makerfield and Scottish by-elections show the limits of Reform's national reach.

stories.title: Dover council by-election: Reform vs Restore Britain vs Tories in three-way fight
stories.summary: Restore Britain is trying to get its first representative elected in a Dover council by-election (Guston, Kingsdown and St Margaret's ward), battling Reform and the Conservatives. The contest will provide insight into how the right-wing vote is being split by the new challenger party.

stories.title: Lords to receive Bank of England digital currency amendment next month
stories.summary: The Treasury will bring an amendment to the Financial Services and Markets Bill in the Lords next month, giving the Bank of England a new legal secondary objective to boost innovation in digital currencies and payments. This is a significant legislative signal on the future of fintech regulation.

stories.title: Early-release scheme final details to come in Lords secondary legislation
stories.summary: Justice Secretary Alex Norris is expected to use secondary legislation (brought through the Lords) to exclude 'unlawful act' manslaughter from the early-release scheme, keeping PC Harper's killers behind bars. However, domestic abusers may still be eligible — over 100 organisations including Women's Aid have written to Burnham warning the scheme contradicts Labour's manifesto pledge.
